rationale: This is the first draft for iteration 0, so there is no race telemetry to learn from. I am using a conservative baseline built from the contract. Five line sensors span 8 cm laterally at 2 cm spacing, with 12 mm footprints on the 25 mm tape, so at least one or two sensors always see the line through the bends. Weights are antisymmetric (+1, +0.5, 0, -0.5, -1) so the signal is zero when centred and has the sign that steers back toward the line. kp=3 gives a moderate correction: a full-tape-edge error of 1 produces about 1050 PWM of wheel differential. ki is small (0.05) to avoid integral windup on curves, and kd=0.5 damps oscillation. base_speed=1.6 (about 80 percent PWM) targets the roughly 1.5 m/s average needed to finish within 3 s, leaving headroom for slowing on tight bends. line_loss='last_direction' lets the robot recover from a lost line by turning toward the side it last saw it. Geometry is a mid-range compact body: wheel_track 0.12 m, wheel_radius 0.03 m, body 0.12 x 0.16 m, mass 0.8 kg. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some oscillation on the slalom. The measurements requested cover all scoring terms so the next iteration can tune kp, kd and base_speed against rms_error and line_loss_events.
